prompt: A panel has a JToggleButton named "mode" and a JLabel named "text". Complete the item listener so the label reads "Good day." while the toggle is unselected and "Yo!" while it is selected.
explanation: A JToggleButton stays pressed until it is clicked again, and every change of its selected state fires an ItemEvent to registered ItemListeners. Inside the listener you ask the button for its current state with isSelected() and push the matching text into the label with setText(). Both doClick() and setSelected(...) change the state, so the listener covers user clicks and programmatic changes alike.
hints: mode.isSelected() tells you whether the toggle button is currently selected.
The listener already runs on every state change -- you only need to set the label text inside it.
A conditional expression works well: text.setText(mode.isSelected() ? "Yo!" : "Good day.");
